messages:
Alex Chen: Quick follow-up on adapter abstraction for hosted/dedicated/private — proposing a probe-first handshake instead of exchanging large manifests on connect. Probe = tiny capability blob (compat_level, feature list, telemetry flags). Goals: faster connects, lower churn, simpler rollouts. Thoughts?

Maya Singh: +1 to probe-first. My concern: asymmetric deployments (private may opt out of telemetry or certain kernels). Probe needs explicit opt-out flags and a stable compat_level so old control plane can reason. @Alex Chen can we make opt-out explicit? :thinking_face: 

Samir Patel: Agree. Also need TTL and invalidation rules for cached probes. If we cache for too long a canary rollout could be invisible. Proposal: default cache TTL = 5m, control-plane push invalidation via webhook or SSE.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for adapter-runtime v3 -> namespace=dedicated-pool-7 :rocket:

Alex Chen: Example minimal probe payload I'm imagining: 
```
{
  "compat_level": 2,
  "features": ["kv_cache","quantized_exec","streaming"],
  "telemetry": "disabled",
  "immutable_id": "adapter-v3-20250401"
}
```
This keeps it tiny but machine-readable.

Maya Singh: Fallback semantics need to be explicit in routing config. If service expects `kv_cache` but adapter reports no `kv_cache`, options: route to variant model, fall back to higher-latency execution, or reject request. Prefer putting policy in route/model config so apps control behavior.

Samir Patel: +1. Suggest `fallbackAction` enum in route config: `["route_variant","degrade_latency","fail_fast"]`. Also record `adapter_mismatch` metric with tags {expected, reported, tenant}.

Alex Chen: Implementation notes I propose: - Probe on initial handshake + heartbeat every 60s (or when capabilities change). - Cache TTL default 5m, tenant-overridable. - Control plane exposes invalidation webhook + direct push to edge. - Emit `adapter_mismatch` and `probe_staleness` metrics.

Maya Singh: :thumbsup: I'll draft a short RFC tomorrow with schema, sample route config, and metric names. Will include migration plan for existing adapters.

Samir Patel: If no objections I'll start a small PoC: adapter exposes `/probe` and control plane caches it + invalidates on canary start. Should be quick.

Alex Chen: No objections. Action items: Maya -> RFC draft, Samir -> PoC, Alex -> telemetry/metrics list. Thanks everyone.
